text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOHA JONE
- More than 50 people were killed or seriously injured across the country on Tuesday, a clear sign that tension and violence are mounting days ahead of early elections.
- President Sali Berisha will give award to controversial Italian ambassador Paolo Foresti. Foresti is leaving Albania amid media allegations he favoured Berisha's Democratic Party.
- OSCE has told Albanian authorities it will withdraw its observers if polling stations were not closed at 1800 hours (local), instead of 2100 as President Sali Berisha wants.
- Paper says Berisha might flee the country before the poll and seek political asylum in a European country.
- Prime Minister Bashkim Fino urged central bank governor Qamil Tusha to give explanations over billion of leks in new bank notes.
- 250 republican guardsmen have resigned after they came under fire from gunmen in Cerrik and Elbasan.
GAZETA SHQIPTARE
- Eight people have been killed and 14 others wounded during an armed conflict caused by a dispute about land in a village of southeastern Albania.

- A policeman and a teenager were killed and six were wounded after a police van and an armoured personnel carrier, which had accompanied Socialist Party leaders on an election tour, were attacked on their way back to Berat by a tank.
- OSCE envoy to Albania Franz Vranitzky said in Washington Albania's early parliamentary elections will not be postponed.
- Socialist Party organisation secretary Namik Dokle managed to address a peaceful rally in his native northern district of Kukes despite being held up by an armed gang.

- President Sali Berisha has told Prime Minister Bashkim Fino he would support the sacking of Finance Minister Arben Malaj, saying he has not taken steps to throw light on the activity of pyramid investment schemes.
ALBANIA
- OSCE envoy Franz Vranitzky said in Washington Albania's new parliament will not deal with the mandate of President Sali Berisha.
- Berisha has asked Fino to take urgent measures to realise the control of pyramid firms in order to fulfil a legal and moral obligation of his government.
INDIPENDENT
- More than 10,000 people poured out to meet Socialist Party leader Fatos Nano in Fier.

- Constitutional Court ruled allowing Democratic Party leader Prec Zogaj to run in elections. "Virginity commission" had prevented Zogaj from running, saying he cooperated with former communist secret police, which Zogaj denied.

- After row between President Sali Berisha and Finance Minister over transparency on pyramid investment schemes, International Monetary Fund decided to discuss the issue with post-election government.
ZERI I POPULLIT
- Hundreds of thousands of people are attending Socialist Party rallies in south and north of the country, a sign that Berisha's days are numbered, paper says.
RILINDJA DEMOKRATIKE
- Armed gangs of the Socialist Party shot in the air over the heads of Democratic Party supporters being addressed by the Democrats' Secretary General Genc Pollo, paper says.
